newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cricket-Pakistan lift ban on opener Sohail.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Pakistan lift ban on opener Sohail.

text.p: Pakistan on Wednesday lifted the two-year playing ban on test opener Aamir Sohail after he apologised over making allegations through the press of match-fixing and betting.
The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) said in a statement the ban had been replaced by a fine of 50,000 rupees ($1,240) for making the allegations against some fellow test players.
Sohail said he was happy with the decision and would be available if asked to join the national team which is currently playing in the four-nation Independence Cup tournament in India.
The PCB statement said Sohail had been given a second chance to appear before a disciplinary committee to prove his allegations.
"I am really happy at being able to resume my profession," Sohail told Reuters but declined to comment on the imposition of the fine.
PCB chief executive Majid Khan said Sohail was eligible to play for Pakistan again but that would depend on the selectors.

Sohail was initially banned from the sport for a month after a row with Majid Khan during a domestic one-day game but he was then given the two-year suspension after going to the press with what the PCB called "baseless charges" of match-fixing and betting.
The lifting of the ban followed what the PCB called an "unconditional apology" in a deal brokered by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's adviser on sports and culture Mushahid Hussain.
Hussain had proposed that the PCB lift the ban after an apology from Sohail, who has played 34 tests, scoring 2,103 runs at an average of 35.64.
